motto: Track inputs, not outcomes. The routine isn't secret; the streak is.
success_bar: Hitting 70% of days = the system is working. Perfection is not the target.

non_negotiables.title: Wake at 7:00 AM, every day, by alarm
non_negotiables.explanation: Not roommate-driven, not motivation-driven. Weekends included (±30 min max). Your 6:30-9:00 wake swing is a rolling mini-jetlag causing most of your grogginess and fog. Fixing the wake time fixes sleep time automatically.

non_negotiables.title: 10-15 min outdoor light within 1 hour of waking
non_negotiables.explanation: Walk, terrace, anything outside. This sets your body clock so you actually feel sleepy at 11 PM instead of 2 AM. At home this means stepping out before evening; in hostel the college walk counts if it's early enough.

non_negotiables.title: Screens off 30 min before bed — paper only
non_negotiables.explanation: Your current pattern is laptop → sleep with zero gap. Last block of the night goes to physical books or notebook (math problems on paper count). This fixes wind-down AND feeds your study roadmap at the same time.

non_negotiables.title: Phone in another room during every deep-work block
non_negotiables.explanation: Your specific failure: checking the phone while waiting for AI responses. The fix is physical distance, not willpower. Phone lives outside the room during blocks, full stop.

non_negotiables.title: One 2-hour GSoC block, 6 days a week
non_negotiables.explanation: 12 h/week — inside your 10-15 h target. Makes output a daily default instead of a deadline panic sprint. Same slot every day so it stops being a decision.

daily_schedule.note: Alarm, not roommates. No feeds for first 30 min.
Non-optional on training days. Eggs / curd + fruit + nuts is enough. One black coffee here is fine.
Phone outside room. While AI generates, eyes stay on the problem — predict the answer.
First 15 min: Anki review of atomic facts. Attempt problems cold before reading. End with 5-min blank-page recall.
After eating: 10 min breath-focus sitting or NSDR track. Boring on purpose. Every 'return to breath' is a focus rep.
Per weekly template below. Easy run = conversational pace — full sentences possible.
Optional. If used, same rules: phone out, recall at the end.
No phone, no podcast, no music. Consolidation + boredom training. Not wasted time.
Physical book or paper problems until lights out.

daily_mind_habits.title: Blank-page recall
daily_mind_habits.when: End of every study block + 2 min each morning recalling yesterday
daily_mind_habits.explanation: Pulling info OUT of your head builds memory; re-reading doesn't. The struggle to remember is the mechanism. Also exposes the gap between 'felt like I learned it' and 'actually know it'.

daily_mind_habits.title: One block at genuine difficulty
daily_mind_habits.explanation: The brain adapts to strain, like muscle to the last hard rep. Confusion during a hard problem IS the treatment working. If the session felt smooth, assume you learned less than it felt like.

daily_mind_habits.title: AI as tutor, never answer machine
daily_mind_habits.explanation: Rules: (1) 10 genuine minutes attempting it yourself first, (2) ask for hints and critique, never solutions, (3) after AI helps, close the chat and reproduce it alone. Research: answer-machine AI users scored 17% WORSE on real exams than students with no AI — while feeling like they learned fine.

daily_mind_habits.title: Feed hygiene
daily_mind_habits.explanation: YouTube app uninstalled, browser-only with Shorts blocked (Unhook extension). No feeds in first 30 min of the day. Breaks between blocks are 10 min of BORING — walk, water, window. Stimulating breaks make re-entering work harder.

daily_mind_habits.title: Naps: 20-30 min max, before 4 PM
daily_mind_habits.explanation: Your 2-hour noon naps steal pressure from night sleep and shift your whole rhythm. If training wrecks you that badly, the training intensity is the problem, not the nap.

weekly.title: Training week: 3× gym, 1-2× badminton, 1× easy run, 1× full rest
weekly.explanation: One activity per day, but by plan not mood. Gym: log every lift every session; progress = weight or reps up every 1-2 weeks. Easy run at conversational pace brings resting HR down. Rest day = walking only — that's where adaptation happens. Right now everything is medium-hard so you never fully recover.

weekly.title: Sunday review — 20 min, on paper
weekly.explanation: Count the week's deep-work blocks and training sessions, find the single biggest leak, change ONE thing. Weekly and on paper because apps didn't stick for you. This is what dissolves the ambition-action stress: visible evidence of process.

weekly.title: One-page Feynman write-up, from memory
weekly.explanation: Every Sunday: explain the hardest thing you learned this week in plain words, no references open. Exposes hollow understanding instantly. Doubles as raw material for the ThinkSwiss application over 6 months.

weekly.title: At least one sharp question to mentors
weekly.explanation: Ask David/Javier real technical questions, share half-finished thinking. Explaining and defending ideas to humans is cognitively demanding in ways solo study isn't. Asking sharp questions is how you look senior, not junior.

nutrition_rules.explanation: Skipping breakfast 3x/week while training daily and taking creatine works against yourself. 5-minute version is fine.
Eggs, dal, paneer, curd, soy chunks (cheapest protein per rupee), whey if budget allows. Target ~1.6 g per kg bodyweight per day.
Keep it. Consistency beats timing. Stay at the top of your 2-3 L water range.
Your one morning black coffee is genuinely good — keep exactly that.
